name: Rufus and his mother
title: Simon of Cyrene's son and wife
summary: Rufus was the son of Simon of Cyrene, the man who was forced to carry Jesus' cross. Rufus and his mother later became known in the early church, and Paul sends them greetings in Romans, where he also calls Rufus' mother his own mother.

keyEvents.title: The Father's Carrying of the Cross
keyEvents.description: Rufus' father Simon of Cyrene was forced by Roman soldiers to carry Jesus' cross to Golgotha. Mark identifies Simon as the father of Alexander and Rufus.

keyEvents.title: Paul's Greeting to Rufus
keyEvents.description: In the closing of Romans, Paul sends greetings to Rufus, whom he calls 'the chosen one in the Lord.' This suggests that Rufus was a well-known and respected believer in the church at Rome.

keyEvents.title: Rufus' Mother as Paul's Mother
keyEvents.description: Paul also greets Rufus' mother and calls her his own mother, showing that she had shown him maternal care and hospitality, perhaps during his missionary journeys.
